evidence.claim: v2 suffix without policy: capability-record-template-v2.yaml shipped alongside v1 with no documented version-bump policy, no deprecation date on v1, no consumer-migration registry. Stripe/Foundry-grade registries pin version policy in code (URI versioning) not filename suffixes.

templates/capability-record-template.yaml still present at HEAD with no deprecation marker

tradeoff_tension: Mechanical cleanup PR shipped fast (44 files, mostly path string updates) and passed schema/eval gates locally — but optimizing for green-CI on a doc-rename let the actual control-plane move (registries/cross-cutting/) get skipped. Speed of cleanup vs. canonical-topology adherence are now in direct conflict; the PR chose speed.
antithesis_steelman: Defense: this is an explicit cleanup-lane A #4 mechanical move, not a topology RFC. Picking registry/ (singular) is consistent with the existing registry/ tree that already houses capabilities/, catalog/, openapi/. Forcing /registries/cross-cutting/ here would have pulled cross-cutting governance into a per-product cleanup PR, violating PR-scope hygiene. The v2 suffix is a transitional dual-publish, not a permanent fork. Hyperscaler URI addressing is an M-CC-P11 Foundry concern, premature here.
synthesis: Two-step: (1) keep PR-15 path choice (registry/capability-templates/) but file an ADR (ADR-0115) within 1 sprint reconciling registry/ vs registries/ — single-noun winner. (2) Add signed-digest + URI-row to artifact-capabilities-registry.json schema before any further template lands; backfill PR-15 rows. The post-merge regression (templates vanished from HEAD) is a P0 fix regardless of which root wins.

principle_violations.note: Templates listed in registry/capability-templates/ at PR-merge are missing from current HEAD. Either a follow-up PR removed them silently or a merge dropped them — public-contract surface changed without ADR/version-bump.
ADR-0069 anchors machine-readable artifacts under /registries/cross-cutting/. PR-15 introduces /registry/capability-templates/ — a fourth competing root.
